newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: OLYMPICS-IOC MAY REVIEW PROCESS OF SELECTING HOST CITIES.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-IOC MAY REVIEW PROCESS OF SELECTING HOST CITIES.

text.p: The International Olympic Committee (IOC) may have to look at ways of cutting the number of cities bidding to host future Olympics, vice-president Dick Pound said on Wednesday.
Eleven cities wanting to host the 2004 Games are being whittled down to four or five final candidates here and Pound said the high numbers made the selection process difficult.
"I don't know about you but I don't have time to visit 11 cities," said Pound.

"You learn something each time you do one of these things and maybe one of the things we learned here is, should there be a pre-pre-selection to keep the number from getting up to something like 11," he said.

Each city was visited by the IOC's 15-member evaluation committee on whose report the 14-member electoral college will shortlist four or five candidates on Friday. All 111 members of the IOC will then vote for their choice on September 5.

Seven cities -- Cape Town, Istanbul, Lille, Rome, San Juan, Stockholm and St. Petersburg -- have complained to the IOC that short-listing the candidates based solely on the evaluation committee's report is unfair.
Some members of the electoral college will make a decision despite having never visited some of the cities.

"In some respects it's not fair because you know 111 IOC members aren't going to go to all the cities," said Pound. "With a smaller number in the final, chances are you might get the visits you need to make your city known."
Pound said that because of the overall high quality of the bids, choices might be based on what was said during Thursday's final presentations to the electoral college and personal experience.

"Tomorrow you'll get more of an injection of the non-technical matter," said Pound. "We have the technical assessment from the evaluation commission and they were careful to deal with technical and factual issues as to abilities of communities to organise games at the level we need.
"Other factors will be that city's experiences in organising events, the political stability, personal experiences and even having attended sports competitions in those counties.
"The way I see it is to mentally think of three baskets: one basket with cities that ought to go forward, another of the ones that aren't ready and the other with ones that are on the bubble."
